title: W-16, W-17, W-19: docs for the public flip (private-repo wording, SECURITY.md, keychain dialog check)
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-16, W-17, W-19 (low). README and runbook say the repository is private and need gh access, and runbook step 6 installs the skill from the private opum-fleet marketplace; there is no SECURITY.md or private reporting route; the runbook teaches the remembering keychain choice without checking the dialog names the intended binary. License (W-37) is the operator's decision and is not part of this task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Install prerequisites and the skill-install route are rewritten for a public repository at the flip
SECURITY.md exists with a private reporting route and a short honest statement of what Ward does and does not defend against
The runbook tells users to check the keychain dialog names the installed binary and explains why it appears after an upgrade
